labels: ARCHIVE CHM Software History Center Focused specifically on collecting and preserving historical software, archives, and oral histories, which makes it ideal for “why this mattered” editorial sections.
ARCHIVE FuzzyMemories A beloved archive of vintage local-TV clips, commercials, station IDs, and broadcast fragments, especially strong for Chicago-area memory lanes.
RECREATION MS-DOS Games on the Internet Archive A very practical entry point for 90s PC gaming nostalgia, especially for browser-playable DOS titles across genres.
ARCHIVE Kid’s Shows on VHS A nostalgic Internet Archive collection for VHS-preserved children’s television, especially good for deep-cut 80s/90s tape-era browsing.
RECREATION Video Game History Foundation Digital Archive Searchable digitized collections of magazines, documents, and ephemera, excellent for citation-grade nostalgia research.
RECREATION Ruffle Open-source Flash emulation for restoring old Flash websites and animations in modern browsers without the original Flash Player.
RECREATION ScummVM One of the best legit tools for replaying classic adventure games and related engines on modern systems, with official compatibility info and some freeware downloads.
ARCHIVE Netlabel Archive Preservation project for web-native music labels and releases, useful if your nostalgia lens includes late-90s/early-2000s internet music culture.
RECREATION MAME A preservation-first emulation framework whose stated purpose is to preserve decades of software history across arcade, console, and computer systems.
ARCHIVE Computer History Museum Collections A high-authority source for digitized artifacts, documents, source code, and archival materials across computing history.
ARCHIVE Version Museum A visual history site covering website, OS, app, and game evolution, especially useful for side-by-side “then vs now” storytelling and product-history rabbit holes.
(Everything I Do) I Do It for You
MARKETPLACE r/oldinternet Small but useful community centered on old forums, defunct sites, internet culture, and the social texture of earlier online life.
RECREATION Flashpoint Archive The most important preservation project for browser games and animations across Flash and many other web technologies, with a huge searchable catalog.
RECREATION noclip.website A digital museum of video game levels that lets you freely explore many classic game maps in-browser, exactly the kind of “walk around your memories” experience users love.
ARCHIVE CHM Oral Histories Firsthand interviews and demonstrations from computing pioneers, perfect for adding depth around the people behind the tools and sites your audience remembers.

ARCHIVE One Terabyte of Kilobyte Age An endlessly fascinating stream of automatically generated screenshots from rescued GeoCities home pages; it is less a search tool and more a pure browse-by-serendipity nostalgia machine.

MARKETPLACE Neocities Browse The browse view of Neocities surfaces current hand-built personal sites by tags, popularity, and recent activity, making it one of the best “living Web 1.0 revival” directories.
RECREATION DOS Games Archive A clean, modern-feeling catalog for classic DOS games with both download and play-online options.
ARCHIVE American Archive of Public Broadcasting Excellent for historic public TV/radio programming, local history, education, arts, and PBS-adjacent research.
LIVING-SITE Radiooooo “The Musical Time Machine” is great for decade-and-country exploration when you want to evoke the sound of a place in the 1990s rather than search one artist at a time.
LIVING-SITE OoCities A long-running GeoCities mirror built from pages saved around the 2009 shutdown, useful when you want direct page-level browsing rather than screenshots or abstract curation.
RECREATION The Emularity / Emulation Station Browser-based emulation stack that powers huge amounts of playable archival software without requiring plugins or local setup.
ARCHIVE GifCities Internet Archive’s GeoCities GIF search engine is one of the best resources for authentic-era animated GIFs, buttons, icons, and page chrome.
You Were Meant for Me / Foolish Games
MARKETPLACE Discogs The biggest music database/marketplace combo in this list and one of the best tools for checking 90s releases, formats, pressings, label connections, and collector demand.
REFERENCE MobyGames A huge, long-running video game database that works well for box art, credits, release history, platform lookup, and “what was that game called?” moments.
RECREATION My Abandonware Huge index of old games by platform and year, very useful for rediscovering half-remembered PC titles.

RECREATION TheOldNet A streamlined portal for accessing old internet archives with a deliberately old-web feel, good for people who want a more “period correct” browsing experience than the standard Wayback interface.
REFERENCE TV Brain A searchable UK television history database covering broadcasts, holdings, and even missing/lost episodes, useful for deeper research rather than casual browsing.
If I Ever Fall in Love
MARKETPLACE r/nostalgia Broader nostalgia community that frequently surfaces defunct websites, commercials, toys, and tech memories from the 1990s.
REFERENCE BBSLIST.TEXTFILES.COM A historical record of BBS numbers and related information, especially good if you want a “pre-web online culture” branch inside your directory.
RECREATION Internet Arcade Internet Archive’s browser-playable arcade collection, focused on coin-op titles from the 1970s through the 1990s via JSMAME.
ARCHIVE Macintosh Garden Excellent archive for classic Mac OS-era games, apps, guides, and community fixes, and especially useful for educational, shareware, and forgotten Mac titles.
RECREATION My 90’s TV A nostalgia TV simulator that recreates the feel of 1990s channel surfing with ads, music videos, movie trailers, shows, and news clips.
ARCHIVE The Vintage Software Collection Internet Archive’s umbrella collection for preserved historical software efforts; useful as a high-level “browse the whole scene” link.
ARCHIVE Web Design Museum A high-value visual archive of thousands of screenshots and videos spanning websites, apps, software, and Flash games from the 1990s onward.
ARCHIVE TEXTFILES.COM A foundational archive of BBS-era and subcultural text material that spills into 1990s online history and early hacker/shareware culture.
RECREATION oldweb.today Lets visitors replay archived sites through emulated historical browsers, which is especially useful if you want to show not just old pages but old rendering behavior.
RECREATION ClassicReload A browser-playable abandonware/preservation site that emphasizes quick access to old DOS, Windows, and console-era software.

MARKETPLACE Archive Team The key volunteer collective for emergency preservation of endangered online content; its wiki is useful both as a resource itself and as a map to what communities are trying to save.
ARCHIVE OldVersion Great for downloading older versions of mainstream programs, browsers, utilities, and games when the nostalgia target is “the software you used,” not just the hardware.
I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)
RECREATION Retromags One of the best destinations for preserved video game magazines, strategy guides, and indexed issue metadata across countries and platforms.
ARCHIVE Paley Archive A serious institutional media archive and catalog for TV, radio, and advertising, with over 160,000 programs and ads in its permanent collection.
RECREATION ProtoWeb A community-driven service that hosts restored historical internet websites and is designed to demonstrate the early web, including on vintage computers.
Candle in the Wind 1997 / Something About the Way You Look Tonight
My Lovin' (You're Never Gonna Get It)
MARKETPLACE ShopGoodwill Online thrift marketplace with enough vintage electronics, media, and oddball household nostalgia to justify inclusion.
RECREATION Space Jam 1996 The canonical surviving 1990s movie promo site, still online with its original sections, graphics, trivia, and “Jam Central” structure.
MARKETPLACE r/90s Active mainstream nostalgia community dedicated specifically to the decade, useful for idea mining and current audience pulse.

LIVING-SITE The Geocities Gallery A restorativland project that visually reassembles archived GeoCities sites by neighborhood, making old homepages feel explorable again instead of buried in raw dumps.
MARKETPLACE r/retrogaming A large community for vintage gaming with a strong CRT, hardware, collecting, and authenticity bent.
MARKETPLACE Reverb If your 90s nostalgia coverage extends into instruments, samplers, pedals, and production gear, Reverb is the best dedicated marketplace in this list.
MARKETPLACE AtariAge Long-running retro community with news, boards, rarity guides, manuals, pictures, articles, and a game database, especially strong for Atari-era collectors.
ARCHIVE Internet Archive TV News Archive Searchable archive of U.S. television broadcasts via closed captioning, ideal for recovering period news language, coverage, and broadcast texture.
RECREATION DOSBox The classic MS-DOS emulator, still essential for reliving 1990s PC games and software in a familiar environment.
MARKETPLACE VOGONS Still one of the best forums for getting old DOS and Windows games working on modern hardware, and a goldmine of compatibility wisdom.
RECREATION OpenEmu Mac-focused all-in-one retro library frontend that auto-organizes ROM backups with box art, making it one of the friendliest nostalgia tools for Apple users.
RECREATION Cameron’s World A collage-style tribute built from GeoCities-era graphics that works as an instant mood-setter for the maximalist, glitter-GIF side of 1990s web memory.
MARKETPLACE Doomworld One of the most important surviving 1990s-born game communities, still central for WADs, mods, mapping, and Doom culture.
REFERENCE MusicBrainz Open music encyclopedia with very strong metadata and a nonprofit/open-data feel that suits archival 90s music research.
Gonna Make You Sweat (Everybody Dance Now)
This Is How We Do It
ARCHIVE TV Ark An online TV museum preserving presentation graphics, idents, promos, titles, commercials, and station branding, with exceptional value for broadcast-design nostalgia.
LIVING-SITE RetroJunk A broad nostalgia site covering commercials, TV, movies, articles, and forums, especially strong for ad breaks, intros, and fan memories.
MARKETPLACE Mercari Useful consumer marketplace for secondhand collectibles, electronics, games, books, and nostalgia-adjacent odds and ends.
ARCHIVE WinWorld One of the strongest software-preservation sites for old Windows, DOS, Macintosh, Amiga, and pre-release software, presented as an online museum.

ARCHIVE Wayback Machine The default first stop for recovering vanished 1990s pages, dead promotional microsites, and old personal homepages through URL and date-based captures.
RECREATION 404PageFound A directory focused on old websites that are still inexplicably alive and largely unchanged, which makes it excellent for “still online from the 90s” roundups.

ARCHIVE Internet Archive The parent digital library behind the Wayback Machine and many of the best vintage media/software collections, useful as a broad discovery hub when you want more than websites alone.
RECREATION WebMuseum One of the earliest still-live web museums, valuable less as a 1990s *subject* archive than as an actual 1990s web artifact that still smells like the early web.
RECREATION Video Game History Foundation Library Catalog The broader catalog for VGHF holdings, including development materials, magazines, artwork, and ephemera beyond what is currently digitized.
MARKETPLACE eBay Nostalgia Toy Box A practical outbound link when your visitors want to turn memory into collecting, especially for toys and hobby items.
REFERENCE Wiby A search engine for older-style, lightweight web pages that feels much closer to browsing the small-web/personal-web ecosystem than modern mainstream search.
You're Makin' Me High / Let It Flow
RECREATION EmulatorJS Useful less as a destination than as a builder tool if you ever want to embed browser emulation directly into 90s.land or a microsite offshoot.
ARCHIVE Internet Archive Software Library The broadest vintage-software umbrella here, pointing to CD-ROM Software, MS-DOS, Vintage Software, Tucows, Shareware CD-ROMs, and more.
ARCHIVE CD.TEXTFILES.COM “The Past on Plastic” is a strong nostalgia link for shareware-CD culture and the weird abundance of late-90s software distribution.
Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men

ARCHIVE Software Heritage A universal source-code archive with real institutional weight, useful when your nostalgia coverage intersects with preservation of software itself rather than just the UX around it.
↗ICQthe ping that makes the web feel social
MARKETPLACE Etsy Vintage Marketplace Good for 90s décor, handmade tributes, repurposed ephemera, and smaller-scale collectible finds that feel more curated than auction-market hunting.
Don't Take It Personal (Just One of Dem Days)
RECREATION VGMaps A long-running archive of ripped and hand-made video game maps, especially useful for 2D-era console and handheld nostalgia.
RECREATION RetroArch A polished frontend for many emulators and game engines, useful if you want a single modern entry point for broad retro play.
ARCHIVE Macintosh Repository A large old-Mac software archive with searchable apps, games, ROM-related materials, and compatibility notes.
ARCHIVE Live Music Archive Stronger for concert nostalgia than radio nostalgia, but still valuable for reliving live recordings and scene history from the late 1990s onward.
RECREATION EmuVR Recreates the “90s bedroom with a CRT and stacks of cartridges” fantasy in VR or 2D mode, which makes it unusually effective as an emotional nostalgia device.
